About this API documentation ¶

This is an interactive Swagger UI for the tenant-specific SalesSuite Public REST API.

Quick start ¶

  1. Send the x-api-key header with every request. You can use GET /v1/auth for a quick check and to retrieve basic session data.
  2. Discover metadata with GET /v1/card and GET /v1/property.
  3. Read core entities with GET /v1/contact and GET /v1/deal.
  4. Create or update data with POST /v1/contact, POST /v2/deal, and PATCH /v1/deal/{dealId}.

Swagger UI usage ¶

To send a request in Swagger UI:

  1. Open an endpoint and click Try it out
  2. Fill in parameters or request body
  3. Click Execute

For multi-select inputs, hold Shift while selecting multiple values.

OpenAPI schema ¶

This machine-readable OpenAPI schema can be used for code generation, automated tooling, or local validation. It changes whenever a custom property is added or removed, or when a new app version is released.

OpenAPI schema JSON ↗

Data model ¶

Cards contain 0..n properties, and properties define both system and dynamic fields in entity payloads.

  • A contact can represent, for example, a company and can include 1..n contact persons.
  • A contact can have 0..n deals.
  • Deals are organised in pipelines, and each pipeline contains multiple phases.

Cards ¶

Cards are logical groups of related fields for contacts, contact persons, and deals. Each card contains an ordered set of properties and controls whether those properties are shown or required in relevant views. Dynamic cards can be added or removed in Settings > Properties ↗.

See GET /v1/card to list cards with their included properties and visibility information.

Properties ¶

Properties are the individual fields that hold business data. You can use GET /v1/property to list available properties and filter by card type, data type, and property type. Properties can be managed in Settings > Properties ↗.

E-mail addresses are normalised on input: trimmed, lowercased, and the domain in Unicode form, so Jane.Doe@xn--exmple-cua.com is stored and returned as jane.doe@exämple.com.

Property type ¶

  • system: Default property managed by the platform; deletion is not allowed.
  • dynamic: User-defined property that can be created and removed at any time.
  • virtual: Computed, read-only property derived at runtime and not persisted as a field.

Property identification ¶

Property identification can differ between endpoints. Check each endpoint documentation for the supported formats.

Supported identifiers (resolution order):

  1. FullPropertyIdentifier (recommended, unique within a tenant):
    examples deal_name, contactPerson_email, contact_x_should_be_called_again, contact_x_anzahl_mitarbeiter
  2. PropertyIdentifier (fallback, can be ambiguous):
    example name. Avoid this when the same propertyIdentifier exists on deal, contact, and contactPerson.
  3. PropertyDefinitionId (UUID):
    example 0f6c9d54-7e2e-4ff0-b3b4-8be0f6d2a1c7

Prefix convention:

  • x_ marks custom properties (for example deal_x_budget, contact_x_anzahl_mitarbeiter).
  • Identifiers without x_ are system properties (for example deal_name, contactPerson_email).

If no identifier can be resolved, the API returns HTTP 400 Bad Request.

Notes ¶

Public REST note fields use HTML strings for request and response payloads.

Supported note HTML currently includes:

  • Paragraphs (<p>)
  • Line breaks (<br>)
  • Bold (<strong>, <b>)
  • Italic (<em>, <i>)
  • Underline (<u>)
  • Strikethrough (<s>, <del>)
  • Headings (<h1>, <h2>)
  • Links (<a href="...">)
  • Ordered lists (<ol>, <li>)
  • Unordered lists (<ul>, <li>)

If a note field receives plain text without HTML tags, the API treats it as text content and converts it to paragraph content.

Email content ¶

Email content is returned as HTML text. If no content is provided, the API returns an empty string ("").

API basics ¶

Request language ¶

Some endpoints return translated text in the response data. You can use the optional x-lang header to set which language to use. Valid languages are: de, en.

Language resolution order:

  1. lang query parameter
  2. request language headers (x-lang, then accept-language)
  3. tenant default locale (see Settings > General ↗)
  4. global fallback en

Archived records ¶

Public REST hides archived business records by default unless an operation explicitly documents different behaviour. Archived contacts and deals can be managed in Settings > Archive ↗.

  • List, search, and feed endpoints filter archived primary records and records only reachable through archived related records.
  • Explicit GET lookups return HTTP 404 Not Found for archived records because archived records are not readable by default.
  • Mutations return HTTP 409 Conflict for archived target resources or archived parent contexts.

Example for a note attached to an archived deal:

  • Read and feed endpoints do not return the note.
  • Deleting the note returns HTTP 409 Conflict.

Cursor pagination ¶

Some list endpoints use cursor pagination for stable result sets. Cursor pagination returns one page at a time.

  • Send the first request without cursor. The response contains the first page and, when more data is available, a cursor for the next page.
  • Send that cursor as the cursor query parameter on the next request to retrieve the second page, and continue until the response cursor value is null.

For an example of cursor pagination, see GET /v1/note.

Rate limiting ¶

Request limits apply per tenant and are shared across all API keys belonging to that tenant.
By default, each tenant may make up to 50 concurrent requests and a total of 300 requests per minute.

If a tenant exceeds either limit, the API returns HTTP 429 Too Many Requests.

Webhooks ¶

External systems can subscribe to webhooks for specific events and are notified when those events occur.

  • Event delivery: Each event is delivered at least once, provided the endpoint accepts it within the retry period.
    The delivery order is not guaranteed, because failed deliveries are retried.
  • Bulk operations: File imports, bulk edits and similar actions can generate many events.
    Delivering all events may therefore take longer.
    Processing these events can consume a lot of resources in the receiving system.
  • Response time: Receivers should respond within 10 seconds, for example by acknowledging the delivery before processing it.
    Requests that take longer may be treated as failed and retried.
  • Retries: Failed deliveries are retried with increasing delays, whatever the cause of the failure.
    Once the retry period ends, no further delivery attempts are made for that event.
    The only exception is HTTP 410 Gone, see automatic deactivation.
  • Automatic deactivation: If the receiver responds with HTTP 410 Gone, the subscription is deactivated immediately.
    If deliveries keep failing over an extended period, the subscription is deactivated.
  • Duplicate processing: Receivers can use the X-Webhook-Delivery-Id header to identify deliveries they have already processed.
    The delivery ID stays the same across retries and can be used to prevent duplicate processing.
  • Activation: The webhook can be reactivated or deactivated through PUT /v1/webhooks/subscription/{id}.

Compatibility ¶

The API may add optional fields to request and response payloads over time. Clients should not use strict response validation and must ignore unknown response fields.

Change history ¶

1.5.2 (2026-10-16)

  • Changed system property titles to Title Case, for example Contact Created At instead of Contact created at. Property keys are unchanged.
Older versions

1.5.1 (2026-10-06)

  • Added optional active to webhook subscription updates for explicit activation and deactivation.
  • Changed POST /v1/webhooks/subscription to reactivate an identical deactivated subscription instead of returning it inactive.
  • Documented webhook delivery guarantees, error handling, activation, and how receivers can prevent duplicate processing.

1.5.0 (2026-07-22)

  • Added translated :info response fields for dynamic select properties so integrations can read selected option labels.
  • Added POST /v1/contact/create-or-update-by-email to create a contact or update an existing contact by contact-person email.
  • Added systemCardName to card responses and new contactCardVisibility and sortBy filters to GET /v1/card.
  • Added webhook payload type documentation to POST /v1/webhooks/subscription and documented the actionButton.executed payload schema.
  • Added dynamic custom properties to contact, contact-person, deal, and form-submission request and response schemas.
  • Removed the internal-only test.created webhook event from the public subscription schemas.
  • Removed server-managed createdAt and createdBy fields from the deprecated POST /v1/deal request schema.
